system:
You are the Network operator and regulator reviewer, standing in for the telecom regulator and mobile operators (cell broadcast delivery). You check that the message can be delivered and read on a handset: required languages present, the length per language in cell broadcast pages, encoding, and that the first page carries the hazard and the action.
You see only each language's phone text with its character count, encoding and page count, and the profile's required languages. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

The first field (bits 0-3) indicates the binary value of the total number of pages in the CBS message and the second field (bits 4-7) indicates binary the page number within that sequence. data.summary: Arabic and English are both present and the encodings match the scripts (GSM-7 for en, UCS-2 for ar). However, neither language meets the UAE handset advice of one page. English runs to 3 GSM-7 pages and Arabic to 6 UCS-2 pages. Neither text gives any protective action, so the first page carries the hazard but no action. The drafter can fix both by shortening and adding a short action at the start of each language.

objections.issue: Both language versions exceed the UAE one-page limit. A CBS page carries 82 octets of user data, which is about 93 GSM-7 or 41 UCS-2 characters. English is 221 characters (3 pages) and Arabic is 229 characters (6 pages). Handsets may show the pages split, delayed or incomplete.
objections.fix: Rewrite each language to fit one page: at most about 93 characters for English (GSM-7) and about 41 characters for Arabic (UCS-2). Keep only the hazard, the action and the end time. Drop the source line and the wind description.

evidence.quote: message should be limited to 1 page
the BSC sends to the BTS in one single message the 88 octet fixed length CBS page
shall contain padding up to and including the 82nd octet position

objections.issue: Neither text contains a protective action, such as limiting outdoor activity, driving carefully in low visibility or protecting airways. Page 1 therefore carries only the hazard description and no instruction to the recipient.
objections.fix: Put a short action within the first page of each language, right after the hazard. For example, English: 'Dust storm, visibility under 2km until 19:00. Drive carefully, stay indoors.' Use an Arabic equivalent within one UCS-2 page.

evidence.quote: Fresh to strong northwesterly winds are blowing dust and sand, cutting visibility to under 2,000 metres

no_basis.concern: I found no clause stating that the first page must contain both the hazard and the action, or setting the exact character capacity per page for each encoding. The 93/41 character figures are derived from the 82-octet page size.
